**Probably yes, but it isn't confirmed yet.**

- Hansen data show 13.5 ha of tree-cover loss in 2025, about 3.9% of the 345.6 ha asset.
- The JRC map shows 98% of that area was forest in 2020, so the loss is on forest that existed after the 2020 baseline.
- The Uruguayan MGAP 2021 forest map classes 13.1 ha as native forest, 0 ha as planted, and 0.4 ha as outside mapped forest. This points to native forest, not plantation harvest.

**Caveat:** The analysis only counts an event as corroborated if a later year is also observed. 2025 is the latest year available, so this event fails that test. It should be treated as provisional until 2026 data confirm the cover didn't regrow. Tree-cover loss also doesn't show the cause, such as clearing, fire or storm damage, so "deforestation" is an inference.
